sources.title: ASAN Visa: Countries eligible for e-visa
sources.publisher: State Agency for Public Service and Social Innovations under the President of Azerbaijan
sources.officialityEvidence: The live ASAN Visa government eVisa service publishes the country eligibility schedule and links to official migration guidance.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Countries eligible for e-visa are listed; marked nationalities have temporary visa-free admission under the stated 2026–27 rules.

sources.title: ASAN Visa: Conditions for issuing electronic visas
sources.publisher: State Agency for Public Service and Social Innovations under the President of Azerbaijan
sources.officialityEvidence: This is the live official ASAN Visa issuance-conditions page for Azerbaijan's electronic visa system.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A standard e-visa is issued within three working days, is single-entry, and permits thirty days’ stay within ninety days.

sources.title: The Migration Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan
sources.publisher: State Migration Service of the Republic of Azerbaijan
sources.officialityEvidence: The English Migration Code is published directly by Azerbaijan's State Migration Service.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Visa-free entry applies under agreements or executive-authority cases; citizens’ entry right is implemented through an Azerbaijani passport.

sources.title: ASAN Visa system started to apply innovations
sources.publisher: State Agency for Public Service and Social Innovations under the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan
sources.officialityEvidence: The official ASAN agency release independently describes the electronic visa as an issued document that applicants apply for, pay for and download.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Obtain an electronic visa with three steps via ASAN Visa: apply, pay and download the eVisa.

sources.title: State Migration Service information on visa-free admission for citizens of certain states
sources.publisher: State Migration Service of the Republic of Azerbaijan
sources.officialityEvidence: The destination's migration authority directly states the ordinary-passport, tourism, date, entry-count and stay conditions for the four-country waiver.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Ordinary passport holders are exempt from 15 February 2026 to 15 February 2027.

sources.title: State Migration Service information on visa-free admission for Bosnia and Herzegovina and Singapore
sources.publisher: State Migration Service of the Republic of Azerbaijan
sources.officialityEvidence: The destination's migration authority directly states the ordinary-passport tourism waiver, dates, entry count and permitted stay for both countries.
sources.supportingExcerpt: From 1 August 2026 to 1 August 2027, the visa requirement is abolished for the named ordinary-passport visitors.

sources.title: Azerbaijan travel advice
sources.officialityEvidence: Singapore's foreign ministry independently confirms the current waiver dates, three-entry limit and 30-day stay for Singapore ordinary-passport citizens.
sources.supportingExcerpt: From 1 August 2026 to 1 August 2027, Singapore citizens may enter Azerbaijan visa-free three times.

policies.title: Azerbaijani citizens’ entry right
policies.summary: The Migration Code implements an Azerbaijani citizen's entry right through that citizen's Azerbaijani passport.
conditions: This citizenship policy does not determine treatment of a foreign passport held by a dual national.
General individual border restrictions or document issues are not represented by passport-nationality status.

policies.title: Temporary visa-free admission for Gulf ordinary passports
policies.summary: Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman and Saudi Arabia have a temporary ordinary-passport visitor waiver from 15 February 2026 through 15 February 2027.
conditions: Visa-free entry is limited to three entries in one year and up to 30 days per entry.
The waiver is for ordinary-passport visitors for tourism; other purposes or longer stays require the relevant visa.
The separate visa-at-airport route for holders of specified third-country residence permits is conditional and is not classified here.
Individual entry restrictions and document requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Temporary visa-free admission for Japanese and Korean ordinary passports
policies.summary: Japan and the Republic of Korea have a temporary ordinary-passport visitor waiver from 1 July 2026 through 1 July 2027.
conditions: Visa-free entry is limited to three entries in one year and up to 30 days per entry.
A valid visa is required at a fourth entry within the stated one-year period.
Individual entry restrictions and document requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Temporary visa-free admission for Bosnian and Singaporean ordinary passports
policies.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina and Singapore have a temporary ordinary-passport visitor waiver from 1 August 2026 through 1 August 2027.
conditions: Visa-free entry is limited to three entries in one year and up to 30 days per entry.
A valid visa is required at a fourth entry within the stated one-year period.
Individual entry restrictions and document requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: ASAN Visa eligible ordinary-passport nationalities
policies.summary: The live ASAN Visa eligibility schedule identifies these nationalities for electronically issued single-entry visitor eVisas.
conditions: The eVisa is electronically issued after ASAN Visa processing; the MFA online application-form portal for consular visas is not itself eVisa issuance.
A standard eVisa is issued within three working days and an urgent eVisa within three hours; it is single-entry, valid for 90 days, and permits a stay of up to 30 days.
The travel document must remain valid for at least three months after eVisa expiry; the approved eVisa must be printed and presented at the border.
The eVisa does not authorize paid work; media activity needs MFA accreditation. Stays over 15 days require registration.
The ASAN schedule's temporary visa-free markings take precedence for the separately dated waiver policies, so those nationalities are excluded here.
